topic: Softmodded Xbox Original Capabilities, video output modes, Region free switching, playing burned discs, auto handling region locked content

softmod_capabilities.heading: Softmod capabilities
softmod_capabilities.research_question: What capabilities does a softmod actually add, and which depend on a specific tool or setup?

video_output_modes.heading: Video output modes
video_output_modes.research_question: Which PAL/NTSC and resolution modes are documented, and what cable, console, and game limits apply?

game_region_switching.heading: Game-region switching
game_region_switching.research_question: How are game-region checks handled, and how does changing video standard differ from game region?

burned_discs.heading: Playing burned discs
burned_discs.research_question: What software and optical-drive conditions affect reading burned game discs?

automatic_handling.heading: Automatic handling of region-locked content
automatic_handling.research_question: Which behaviors are automatic, which need manual configuration, and how do game and DVD-movie regions differ?

references.title: Xbox Softmodding Tool README
supported_claims: Rocky5’s specific softmod advertises unsigned-code execution, NKPatcher settings, dashboard and softmod repair, and a video-region setting.
The README says the tool supports all Xbox versions, but does not establish that every feature behaves identically on every console or configuration.
references.evidence_summary: The project README directly lists the tool’s features and describes NKPatcher as the component that patches the kernel and enables unsigned code. It documents NTSC/PAL video-setting options and notes component cable use for HD resolutions. These are claims about this tool, not every softmod.
references.fact_check_notes: Independently opened and checked. Current README content directly supports the project-specific claims; the broad all-versions statement is the project’s own claim, not an independent compatibility test.

references.title: Xbox: Frequently Asked Questions
supported_claims: The FAQ describes exploiting the console as enabling homebrew and says game backups can be played without region locks.
The FAQ says a PAL Xbox can be switched to NTSC with Enigmah-X for access to 720p and 1080i; it also says modded dashboards can choose a game’s highest supported resolution and the correct region.
references.evidence_summary: The independently checked FAQ distinguishes region selection and video resolution in its guidance. It is community-maintained and gives an overview, not a complete compatibility matrix or proof that every dashboard/setup handles every title automatically.
references.fact_check_notes: Independently opened and checked. The supplied URL redirects to the canonical page with decoded punctuation; no substantive correction needed. The FAQ supports the claims as community guidance, with setup-specific limits.

references.title: Xbox: DVDROM
supported_claims: The page’s drive-by-media table reports that optical-drive models differ in their compatibility with CD-R, CD-RW, DVD-R, and other media.
The table characterizes compatibility as variable, including media that works with most or some media, rather than guaranteed for every drive.
references.evidence_summary: The checked page contains a drive-model/media-type compatibility table and legend. This supports the claim that burned-disc reading depends on drive model and media. It does not, in the checked content, establish detailed burning-software requirements, condition-related failure rates, or generic-drive dashboard/eject limitations.
references.fact_check_notes: Independently opened and checked. The page supports drive/media variation, but the supplied broader claims about drive condition, failures, and replacement behavior were not established by the checked material.

references.title: Xbox Hardware Design Specification
supported_claims: The specification documents TV-encoder output modes including NTSC-M, NTSC-J, PAL-I, PAL-M, PAL-60, and component HDTV output.
The specification lists component HDTV modes of 480p, 720p, and 1080i, while noting VGA is for development and not officially supported in retail Xbox.
references.evidence_summary: The independently checked PDF’s video-output section and conversion matrix list supported signal families and HDTV modes. The document describes hardware capability; it does not show that every retail console, cable, game, or television can use every mode.
references.fact_check_notes: Independently opened and checked. This is a primary technical document hosted by a community wiki; the host does not change the document’s stated scope or prove universal retail usability.

references.title: Original Xbox EEPROM data structures
supported_claims: The repository identifies a DVD-region-lock setting in the Xbox EEPROM separately from other configuration data.
The repository does not establish how a particular softmod or playback application enforces or changes DVD-movie-region behavior.
references.evidence_summary: The checked EEPROM field table lists a DVD Region setting and labels its initial origin as unknown. The repository also documents separate region flags. This supports distinguishing the DVD-region field from general video-mode discussion, but does not independently establish practical playback behavior.
references.fact_check_notes: Independently opened and checked. Retained the supplied GitHub URL. Its technical documentation is useful for the EEPROM-field distinction, but should not be treated as proof of application-level behavior.

references.title: NKPatcher config.inc
supported_claims: The inspected source defines GAME_REGION_AUTO but comments it out by default.
It describes choosing a region from the executable header when enabled.
references.evidence_summary: Manually checked against the linked source during post-run review.
references.fact_check_notes: Source-file configuration, not proof of a compiled release setting.

references.title: Xbox: Upgrading your hard drive
supported_claims: The guide describes using an EEPROM backup and a lockable replacement drive on a softmodded Xbox.
references.evidence_summary: Manually checked against the linked source during post-run review.
references.fact_check_notes: Community procedure requiring hardware and software beyond the softmod.

references.title: Official AvaLaunch Manual, version 2.2
supported_claims: The manual describes choosing PAL or NTSC with the Enigmah VideoMode Switchdisc and rebooting.
It says to burn the utility onto media that boots on the user’s Xbox.
references.evidence_summary: Manually checked against the linked source during post-run review.
references.fact_check_notes: A specific utility procedure, not a universal softmod feature.

references.title: Xbox executable data structures: XBE.cs
supported_claims: The source lists game-region flags and executable certificate fields.
references.evidence_summary: Manually checked against the linked source during post-run review.
references.fact_check_notes: Technical structure description, not proof of a particular game’s behavior.

generation_references.title: DVD_REGION structure
supported_claims: Microsoft’s general DVD-device documentation distinguishes the region code of mounted DVD media from the DVD player’s system-region code.
generation_references.evidence_summary: The Microsoft documentation defines separate media-region and player-region fields in a DVD playback-control structure. It supports the general distinction between DVD movie-region checks and other console-region settings, but is not Xbox-specific.
generation_references.fact_check_notes: Independently opened and checked. The page is current as displayed and directly supports the general DVD-region distinction, not Xbox-specific softmod behavior.

generation_outline.key_claim: A softmod can enable unsigned-code execution and homebrew, but additional settings and repair features depend on the specific softmod package.
generation_outline.caveat: Rocky5’s listed features are specific to that tool; community FAQ descriptions are not a compatibility guarantee for every setup.
generation_outline.heading: Softmod capabilities

generation_outline.key_claim: The Xbox hardware specification documents PAL/NTSC-family output and component HDTV modes up to 1080i, while usable modes depend on configuration, cable, and game support.
generation_outline.caveat: Hardware capability alone does not establish that every retail console, game, cable, or display supports every mode.
generation_outline.heading: Video output modes

generation_outline.key_claim: Game-region handling and video-standard selection are distinct: modded systems may bypass game region locks, while a tool such as Rocky5’s offers a separate PAL/NTSC video setting.
generation_outline.caveat: Behavior can depend on the game, dashboard, and softmod configuration; do not equate changing video standard with changing game region.
generation_outline.heading: Game-region switching

generation_outline.key_claim: Burned-disc readability varies by Xbox optical-drive model and media type; the checked sources do not establish a universal software or burning procedure.
generation_outline.caveat: The drive/media table is community-maintained and does not establish how wear, recording quality, or every software setup affects results.
generation_outline.heading: Playing burned discs

generation_outline.key_claim: A community FAQ reports that modded dashboards can select a game’s correct region and highest supported resolution automatically, while DVD-movie region is a separate playback-control setting.
generation_outline.caveat: Automatic game handling is not established for every dashboard/setup; the DVD-region sources do not show that softmods automatically bypass movie-region checks.
generation_outline.heading: Automatic handling of region-locked content

post_run_review.method: Manual source review and draft revision after the recorded model run
post_run_review.excluded_original_source: Microsoft Learn DVD_REGION structure; general Windows DVD-device documentation did not directly establish Xbox behavior.
